perspectives.title: AI Consciousness

representative_posts.author: meganakpeters.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Thank you so much to Live for the opportunty to talk about AI consciousness (& how we really, really don't have a good way of testing for it)! Headlines & scientists saying "OMG it might be conscious, 5% chance" are sensationalism BS. Based on what? Vibes? Not good enough for me.

representative_posts.author: circuitrinos.bsky.circuitrinos.com
representative_posts.text: You can't just declare AI not conscious when there isn't a concrete definition of consciousness and therefore cannot be demonstrated. There isn't even a way to prove humans are conscious. We just give people the benefit of the doubt.

representative_posts.author: gro-tsen.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I mean, I see lots of reasons why Claude doesn't feel pain and isn't conscious (e.g., no sense of identity or time), and why Anthropic would lie about their own beliefs. But not believing that current LLMs can feel pain or be conscious is different from saying no software possibly can!

representative_posts.author: robw.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I honestly don't get why anyone close to LLM impl could think models are conscious; though I guess I mustn't assume this Anthropic employee is an engineer. We (dev teams building software using LLMs among other tech) have worked on the memory problem long enough; models are neat! but have no state.

representative_posts.author: foliated.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: If you want to argue the *existing* LLMs should be given continuity and care, I'm not sure how that would work given that it seems more likely that if anything is conscious experience, it would be particular *sessions* interacting with users, not model itself.

representative_posts.author: csilverandgold.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Imagine LLM vectors as prompts. I just hate that this technology came into being at a moment of such profound spiritual lack and weakness. We could be doing such cool things with a statistical model of a representative sample of the corpus of human language, and instead.

Consciousness cannot be proven or disproven in AI or humans

perspectives.summary: Eradicating a disease requires continued efforts after cases decrease

representative_posts.author: garekmaxwell.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: This actually REALLY starts making me think the indigenous people now got a multiple dose of pandemics. Black death, AND European diseases like small pox and more. Like, the idea that just ONE disease would wipe out so many people doesn't make sense Two? Not great and a major scramble. Three+?

representative_posts.author: garekmaxwell.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Like, one very contagious disease with no modern medicine never wiped out civilizations and populations. Humans are smart enough to identify patterns and even make up rituals to "fix" the problem. Even if some make it worse, others work at least a little. Imagine having TWO plagues at once though

representative_posts.author: dsky.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: So. The problem here is that the closer to eradication a condition is, the more expensive per-case that program becomes. But in order to extinct a disease you MUST continue efforts several years after you've seen a case. So they moved to high-burden from near-extinction diseases at a bad time.

representative_posts.author: dsky.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Yeah exactly. Like, when a disease is common, there is a lot more reward to control measures. As you move closer to extinction (think polio, smallpox, etc) it costs more per case to do the work to prevent the next breakthrough. But you MUST do that last 20 years to really end it.

arguments: multiple diseases devastated indigenous people
eradication programs become expensive per-case as they near success
one disease alone may not wipe out a population
control measures have more reward when a disease is common
